title: pricing-boundaries-sso-rbac-contract-clauses-experiment
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and run a pricing + contract experiment that clarifies when SSO/SAML and RBAC are treated as included features vs paid add-ons, and produce a contract language pack and security questionnaire guidance for sales/legal. Outcome: a repeatable packaging decision framework and a short-run pricing experiment to validate willingness-to-pay and sales friction.
background: Multiple enterprise prospects request SSO/SAML + fine-grained RBAC as explicit contractual commitments. Legal and Sales need consistent language and guardrails (implementation timelines, support commitments, pricing). Current ambiguity causes long procurement loops and ad-hoc concessions. Prior PM tickets outlined the security commitments matrix but did not tie to pricing experiments or standardized contract language.
goal: Ship a contract clause library + pricing experiment that: (1) establishes whether SSO/SAML is part of 'Enterprise' baseline or an add-on in >50% of negotiations; (2) quantifies price uplift and sales close impact for RBAC as a committed SLA; (3) produces approved security questionnaire canned answers and a one-page implementation SLA to include in term sheets.
acceptance_criteria: Legal-approved contract clause templates for: SSO/SAML included, SSO as add-on, RBAC commitment clause
A 6-week pricing experiment plan with 3 cohorts (baseline, include-SSO, add-on-SSO+RBAC) and measurement plan
At least 5 sales cycles run in experiment with documented customer feedback
Security questionnaire mapped to standard answers for top-10 enterprise controls and cross-referenced to our Private/Dedicated offering
Go/no-go decision documented and next steps for rollout (packaging change + billing SKU updates)
decisions: Experiment splits agreed: Cohort A (current packaging), Cohort B (SSO included in Enterprise list price), Cohort C (SSO included + RBAC committed with 6-month SLA, price uplift)
RBAC guarantee limited to configuration-level RBAC for Redwood Console and API keys; database-level row-level permissions deferred to customer implementation
Implementation SLA windows: 90 days for Hosted/Dedicated, 180 days for Private (on-prem) — to be reflected in contract clause
Security questionnaire canned answers will reference existing SOC2 and provide additional items specific to VPC/Private deployments rather than promise new controls

risks: Large enterprise customers expect immediate RBAC parity with existing on-prem systems; overpromising will lead to delivery delays
Price uplift could lengthen sales cycles and reduce conversion in mid-market segment
Ambiguous contract language could lead to one-off concessions and inconsistent billing
next_steps: Finalize clause templates and circulate for Legal sign-off by 2025-03-21
Instrument analytics events for cohort tracking (close-rate, time-to-close, ACV) — ENG/Analytics owners assigned
Run 6-week experiment starting 2025-03-24 with at least 5 active sales deals per cohort
Pull together a short 'sales play' and FAQ for SDRs/AEs explaining trade-offs and negotiation guidance
notes_for_sales: Use 'SSO included' language only if deal is above $250k ACV for first-year pricing in cohort B
For cohort C, present RBAC as a committed deliverable with a defined acceptance checklist and 6-month roadmap
Offer implementation consulting bundle as optional add-on for Private deployments to reduce delivery risk
